summary: Vitamin B12 supports blood and nerve cells and DNA production.

functions.title: Physiological role
functions.description: Vitamin B12 supports blood and nerve cells and DNA production.

functions.title: Food context
functions.description: Animal foods and specifically fortified foods provide B12; unfortified plant foods do not naturally supply it.

referenceValues.notes: FDA label reference for adults and children aged 4+. Not a personalised target, EAR, RDA or UL.

foodSourceRules.notes: Comparable source-backed composition per 100 g; not a health score or a measure of individual absorption.

absorptionFactors.description: Absorption of food-bound B12 involves release from protein and intrinsic factor; some conditions or medicines interfere with this process.

deficiency.overview: Vitamin B12 deficiency can cause megaloblastic anaemia or nerve problems; nerve damage can occur even without anaemia.
deficiency.medicalBoundary: Symptoms are nonspecific and cannot diagnose a nutrient deficiency. Diagnosis may require clinical evaluation and appropriate laboratory testing.

excess.overview: NIH ODS reports no demonstrated harm from high B12 intake; this is not a reason to use high doses or change medication.
excess.medicalBoundary: An upper limit is not an intake goal. Seek medical or professional advice before changing supplement or medication use.
